cosas.cosa: A mature broadleaf oak tree of a medieval north-European woodland, about 9 metres tall: a thick gnarled bark-covered trunk with a slight lean, roots gripping the ground at its foot, strong spreading branches and a broad rounded crown made of dense clumps of small leaves.

A young slender broadleaf tree about 4 metres tall: a thin straight trunk no thicker than a wrist, a few thin side branches and a small, sparse, airy crown of leaves; clearly young and lightweight, easy to fell with a stone axe.
A wild hazel bush about 1.4 metres tall: many thin upright woody stems growing from one point in the ground, with rounded clumps of soft green leaves.

A low wild berry bush about 1.2 metres tall, a dense rounded mass of small dark green leaves on woody twigs, with gaps among the leaves where bunches of berries hang (draw it with NO berries: only leaves and twigs).
A low tangled thicket of wild scrub about 0.9 metres tall and 1.5 metres wide: thorny bramble stems, dry twigs and small leaves, the kind of undergrowth that has to be cleared with an axe.
A medium weathered limestone boulder about 0.9 metres tall, irregular rounded shape with cracks, lichen patches and a little moss at its base; big enough to be broken apart with a stone maul.
